In semiarid
environments with inadequate water (< 1000 mm rainfall yr–1) and on acid
infertile soils, hedgerows produce too little biomass and/or become too
competitive to benefit crops. If (C) is substantially reduced, HI may increase
crop yields in some of these situations, even for a relatively small (F), but
the necessary management of hedges could be too intensive to be practical.

quote:
In the zones
furthest from sources of propagules and/or dominated by invasive
species, planting native species of diﬀerent functional groups can be an
eﬀective strategy for accelerating the recovery of the structure and of
certain species of the TMCF, while in the zones adjacent to mature
forests, recovery of some structural characteristics can take place with
the simple exclusion of disturbance.

relationship.requirement: Passive recovery through disturbance exclusion is supported in zones adjacent to mature forest; distant propagule-source zones may need active planting.
relationship.note: Direction means nearer forest favours passive strategy selection, not fitted distance-response or hard limit.

context.practice_as_described: Passive forest restoration through excluding disturbance in former pastures of tropical montane cloud forest, Veracruz Mexico. Author inference from one21year comparison; regeneration and soil processes may still require later intervention. Distance observations remain context, not thresholds.
context.note: User-mandated T4 targeting gate passed. Qualitative regional siting evidence only; no numeric curve, global exclusion, implementation approval or effect extraction.

quote:
In the South
Caucasus, two natural limits restrict forest expansion: at 2.300-2.600m a.s.l. the upper tree
line is visible, whereas steppe and semi-desert ecosystems form the lower tree line.

relationship.requirement: South Caucasus forest expansion is restricted by an upper treeline in the regional altitude band stated in the quote; steppe and semidesert ecosystems form lower treeline.
relationship.note: Regional upper-bound band, not exact universal exclusion cutoff; lower boundary not numerically specified. No general monotonic direction or executable function inferred.

context.practice_as_described: High-altitude community afforestation for erosion control, Armenian South Caucasus. Quote concerns regional natural forest limits, not report that planting occurred1900–2300m. Source no explicit local calibration or provenance for treeline; human review required.

quote:
Overlaying the results of this study 
with those of the China_LUCC for 2020 showed that 8795.5 km2 of potential wetlands in China 
were anthropogenically occupied and unsuitable for wetland restoration. The second national wet­
land resources survey also shows that infrastructure occupation has become one of the five major 
threat factors affecting the change in wetlands in China, and it has permanent effects. Therefore, 
when considering wetland restoration, the first step is to mask off the existing built-up land area 
from the results.

relationship.note: Source explicitly masks built-up land from modelled potential wetlands before selecting restoration areas. No numerical suitability score or automatic global mask.

context.practice_as_described: Wetland restoration on modelled potential wetland locations currently converted to cropland, grassland or woodland. Existing built-up land is excluded before mapping restoration targets. Baseline is current land cover rather than experimental treatment.
context.note: Section4.3 PDF17 and Figure9: a spatial implementation gate, not occurrence-only evidence. Modelled potential wetlands are overlaid with China_LUCC2020. Native source cites8795.5km2 anthropogenically occupied potential wetlands as unsuitable; existing built-up area is the explicit exclusion class. Do not generalize that every anthropogenic use is excluded: cropland is an explicit restoration target(PDF18). Woodland conversion has ecological tradeoffs acknowledged by authors. Source screen does not establish former wetland history pixel-by-pixel, landowner feasibility, legal status or global applicability. Retain unapproved scoping evidence; no runtime mask activated. No species/crop envelope.

model_use.method: Overlay potential wetland model with current land cover; remove existing built-up area

justification_quote:
Figure 9a shows the spatial distribution of potential suitable areas for wetland restoration, with 
the results of this study indicating potential wetlands and remote sensing results indicating crop­
land, grassland, or woodland.
